title: Binary Formats — Where It Stands
thesis: The one pilot page that rates a plan, not a product: the binary plane is 607 lines of design and zero shipped code -- no classes, no decode engine, no tests, no phase has run. The bet is to treat a binary file as 'a table the bytes forgot to show', decoded in one engine crossing into the stzTable analysis stack that already exists, with zero new DLLs; the substrate is real, everything above it is named, sequenced (BN0-BN5) and unbuilt.

lanes.note: stzBytes over an engine handle buffer plus hex/base64/crc32; the bridge silently truncates slices above 4096/8192 bytes and has no typed endian readers
stzBinarySchema (pure-Ring data, never code) consumed by a planned stz_bytes_decode_records that decodes the whole file in one crossing; no code (BN1)
Planned :U8..:U64, :I8..:I64, :F32/:F64 in both endiannesses; the engine has only stz_bits_byte_swap, no readInt or endian-aware scalar decode
UTF-8 is codepoint-correct today, but the EBCDIC CP037 / CP500 / CP1140 translation tables the plan targets do not exist
Planned :PackedDecimal (COMP-3) and :Zoned (overpunch) decode, the numeric heart of COBOL data; no code, no primitive
Planned stzCopybook compiling a copybook into a stzBinarySchema (BN2); two fossils exist and the plan disavows both
Planned flat fields + :occurs first, then :variants (REDEFINES), RDW variable-length records and Fortran framing; nothing built, staged to v2 (BN4)
The destination (stzTable with stats, Tukey, plots, CSV/JSON, SQLite) is real; the pipe into it does not exist because nothing decodes yet
Planned stzBinaryFileMaker + Narrate() and stz_bytes_encode_records (BN3) so a read schema also writes; no code
Planned HexView(), DecodeReport(), Explore() and streaming (BN4); file I/O today is whole-file only via stz_file_read, no seek/chunk

standouts: A declarative data schema decoded in one engine crossing, not a generated parser (vs Kaitai's compiler model)
Decoded bytes land in stzTable, the same analysis stack as every other Softanza source
Round-trip: the same schema vocabulary reads and writes, which most binary parsers cannot do
Zero new DLLs: extend the stz_bytes engine rather than vendor Kaitai
gaps: Repair the byte-bridge truncation (fixed [4096]/[8192] return buffers)
Endian readers + EBCDIC CP037, then wire decode into stzTable
COBOL copybook compiler (BN2), tied to the RINGBOL commercial gate
